rules.title: Drive {name}
rules.what: The root of this drive.
rules.why: Everything on the drive lives under here.

rules.title: {name}
rules.what: A folder at the top level of the drive. These are usually created by you, an installer, a game launcher or a driver package.

rules.title: Windows
rules.what: The Windows operating system: the kernel, drivers, built-in apps, fonts and everything Windows needs to boot.
rules.why: Your PC won't start without it. Never delete things in here by hand — use the clean-up actions SpaceScope offers for the few parts that are safe to shrink.
rules.note: Only Temp, logs, crash dumps and update caches inside Windows are safe to clear.

rules.title: {name} (core Windows files)
rules.what: The core 64-bit (System32) and 32-bit (SysWOW64) programs and libraries of Windows.
rules.why: Essential. Deleting anything here can stop Windows from booting.

rules.title: Driver Store
rules.what: A copy of every driver package ever installed — including old graphics drivers, which are 1–2 GB each.
rules.why: Windows installs devices from here. Old versions let you roll back a driver.
rules.note: Advanced: old driver versions can be removed with `pnputil /delete-driver oemXX.inf` or the free tool DriverStore Explorer. Don't delete files manually.

rules.title: Windows component store (WinSxS)
rules.what: Every version of every Windows component, kept so updates can be installed, repaired and uninstalled. Much of it is hard-linked into System32, so it looks bigger than it really is (SpaceScope counts shared files only once).
rules.why: Required for Windows Update and for repairing Windows.
rules.note: Never delete files here. 'Windows Update clean-up' (DISM component clean-up) safely removes superseded versions — typically 1–5 GB. Takes a few minutes.

rules.title: Windows Installer cache
rules.what: Copies of the .msi/.msp installers of every installed program and patch.
rules.why: Needed to repair, update or uninstall those programs. Deleting files here leaves programs you can never cleanly remove or patch.

rules.title: Installer patch baseline cache
rules.what: Baseline copies of files used when applying patches to Office and other MSI programs.
rules.why: Without it, future patches may ask for the original install media.
rules.note: Leave it unless you're desperate for space.

rules.title: Windows temporary files
rules.what: Scratch files that Windows services and installers write while they work.
rules.why: Only needed while the program that created them is running.
rules.note: Files currently in use are skipped automatically.

rules.title: Windows log files
rules.what: Diagnostic logs from Windows setup, updates (CBS), servicing and other components. The CBS log folder can grow to several GB.
rules.why: Only useful for troubleshooting a specific failure.

rules.title: Component servicing logs (CBS)
rules.what: Logs from Windows Update and DISM. Old ones are compressed into CbsPersist_*.cab files that can pile up.
rules.why: Troubleshooting only.

rules.title: Windows Update data
rules.what: Windows Update's working folder: the update history database and downloaded update packages.
rules.why: Windows Update uses it constantly.

rules.title: Downloaded Windows updates
rules.what: Update packages Windows has downloaded. After updates are installed these are just leftovers.
rules.why: Windows re-downloads anything it still needs.
rules.note: If an update is installing right now, wait until it finishes.

rules.title: Delivery Optimization cache
rules.what: Copies of Windows and Store updates kept so they can be shared with other PCs on your network or the internet.
rules.why: Purely a sharing cache — your PC doesn't need it.

rules.title: Prefetch
rules.what: Records of how programs load, used by Windows to start them faster.
rules.why: Deleting it just makes apps start a little slower until it is rebuilt. Small — not worth clearing.

rules.title: Crash dumps (blue screens / driver hangs)
rules.what: Memory snapshots written when Windows crashed (blue screen) or a driver like the GPU driver hung. LiveKernelReports can hold multi-GB files.
rules.why: Only useful if you're debugging those crashes.

rules.title: Full system crash dump
rules.what: A copy of RAM saved during the last blue screen. Can be as large as your memory.
rules.why: Only for debugging that crash.

rules.title: Installed fonts
rules.what: Every font installed for all users.
rules.why: Apps and Windows itself render text with these. Remove fonts via Settings → Personalization → Fonts.

rules.title: {name} (Windows)
rules.what: Part of Windows itself.
rules.why: Required by Windows.

rules.title: Windows Search index
rules.what: The database that makes Start-menu and Explorer search instant.
rules.why: Can be rebuilt (Settings → Searching Windows → Advanced indexing options → Rebuild), but search is slow until it finishes. Delete via that button, never by hand.

rules.title: Microsoft Defender data
rules.what: Antivirus definitions, quarantine and scan history.
rules.why: Keeps your antivirus working.

rules.title: Windows Error Reporting files
rules.what: Crash reports and memory dumps collected when apps stop responding, queued to send to Microsoft.
rules.why: Not needed by you or Windows.

rules.title: Windows diagnostic/telemetry logs
rules.what: Event-trace (.etl) logs used for diagnostics and the Update Orchestrator.
rules.why: Troubleshooting only.

rules.title: Page file (virtual memory)
rules.what: Overflow memory: Windows moves rarely-used RAM here so your apps never run out of memory.
rules.why: Required for stability, and for crash dumps. Windows sizes it automatically.
rules.note: You can't delete it while Windows runs. It can be resized under System Properties → Advanced → Performance → Virtual memory, but leaving it on automatic is recommended.

rules.title: Swap file (Store apps)
rules.what: Used by Windows to suspend and resume Microsoft Store apps.
rules.why: Managed by Windows; tied to the page file.

rules.title: Hibernation file
rules.what: Holds the contents of your RAM when the PC hibernates. Fast Startup also uses it. It's often 40% of your RAM size.
rules.why: Only needed if you use Hibernate or Fast Startup.
rules.note: Turning hibernation off deletes this file instantly. You lose Hibernate and Fast Startup (boot may be a few seconds slower). Re-enable any time with `powercfg /hibernate on`.

rules.title: System Volume Information (restore points)
rules.what: System Restore points, Volume Shadow Copies and indexing data. Hidden and locked to everyone but SYSTEM.
rules.why: System Restore points let you roll Windows back after a bad driver or update.
rules.note: Don't touch the folder. To shrink it, open System Protection → Configure: lower 'Max Usage' or delete old restore points.

rules.title: Recycle Bin
rules.what: Files you deleted. They still take up space until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
rules.why: Lets you restore something you deleted by mistake.
rules.note: Emptying it is permanent. Glance through it first (it opens in Explorer).

rules.title: Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)
rules.what: Your previous version of Windows, kept after a major upgrade or reset so you can go back.
rules.why: Only needed to roll back the upgrade. Windows deletes it automatically after about 10 days.
rules.note: Removing it means you can't go back to the previous Windows version. Use Disk Cleanup → 'Previous Windows installation(s)', which handles the locked permissions.

rules.title: Windows upgrade leftovers ({name})
rules.what: Temporary files from a Windows feature upgrade, reset or recovery-environment update.
rules.why: Only needed during the upgrade itself.
rules.note: Use Disk Cleanup → 'Temporary Windows installation files' / 'Windows upgrade log files' to remove them cleanly.

rules.title: Windows setup files (ESD)
rules.what: Windows installation images downloaded by the Media Creation Tool or an upgrade.
rules.why: Not needed once Windows is installed.

rules.title: Mac / Linux trash on this drive
rules.what: Files that were deleted on a Mac (or Linux PC) while this drive was plugged into it. They went to this hidden trash folder instead of being erased, and Windows never shows them.
rules.why: Only useful if you want to recover something you deleted on that computer.
rules.note: Deleting it permanently erases those already-deleted files.

rules.title: macOS system data ({name})
rules.what: Search index and file-tracking data a Mac wrote to this drive.
rules.why: Useless on Windows; a Mac recreates it if needed.

rules.title: macOS metadata files
rules.what: Folder-view settings (.DS_Store) or resource-fork shadow files (._name) a Mac creates next to real files.
rules.why: Useless on Windows; the real file is unaffected.

rules.title: Installer rollback data
rules.what: Rollback files Windows Installer keeps while (un)installing programs.
rules.why: Should be empty unless an install is in progress or crashed.

rules.title: Recovered file fragments (CHKDSK)
rules.what: Fragments of damaged files that CHKDSK salvaged after a disk error, saved as FILE*.CHK.
rules.why: Rarely recoverable into anything useful.

rules.title: {name} (boot & recovery)
rules.what: Boot loader and Windows Recovery Environment files.
rules.why: Needed to start Windows and to repair it.

rules.title: Crash-dump stack log
rules.what: A small log Windows keeps for writing crash dumps.
rules.why: Tiny; Windows recreates it at boot.

rules.title: Performance logs
rules.what: Reports from Performance Monitor. Almost always empty.
rules.why: Not needed.

rules.title: Extracted driver installers ({name})
rules.what: Unpacked copies of GPU/chipset driver installers. The driver itself is already installed in Windows.
rules.why: Only used during installation.

rules.title: {name} (installer copies)
rules.what: Installer or driver copies placed by your PC maker, Office or OneDrive.
rules.why: Occasionally used to reinstall or repair; usually unnecessary.

rules.title: {name}
rules.what: Where installed desktop programs live.
rules.why: Remove programs with Settings → Apps → Installed apps, not by deleting their folders.

rules.title: {name} (installed program)
rules.what: The program files of {name}.
rules.why: Needed to run {name}. Deleting the folder breaks the app and leaves junk in the registry.
rules.note: Don't need it? Uninstall it from Settings → Apps so it's removed properly.

rules.title: Common Files
rules.what: Components shared by several programs (runtimes, codecs, licensing services).
rules.why: Removing them breaks the programs that use them.

rules.title: Microsoft Store apps
rules.what: Installed Microsoft Store and built-in apps (and Game Pass games installed on this drive).
rules.why: Locked by Windows. Uninstall apps via Settings → Apps.

rules.title: ProgramData (shared app data)
rules.what: Hidden folder where programs keep data shared by all users: licences, databases, downloaded content, caches.
rules.why: Programs depend on it — look at individual subfolders.

rules.title: {name} (shared app data)
rules.what: Data {name} keeps for all users on this PC.
rules.why: May contain settings, licences or downloaded content for {name}.
rules.note: If {name} is no longer installed, this is probably a leftover and can be removed.

rules.title: Installer package cache
rules.what: Installer copies kept by Visual Studio, .NET, C++ runtimes and other Burn-based installers.
rules.why: Used to repair, modify and uninstall those programs. Deleting it can make them impossible to uninstall cleanly.
rules.note: Not recommended to clear by hand.

rules.title: Visual Studio installer cache
rules.what: Downloaded Visual Studio components kept for repairs and modifications.
rules.why: Visual Studio Installer re-downloads what it needs.
rules.note: Close Visual Studio Installer first.

rules.title: Epic Games vault cache
rules.what: Downloaded Unreal Engine marketplace assets.
rules.why: Re-downloaded when you add them to a project again.

rules.title: User profiles
rules.what: One folder per Windows account on this PC.
rules.why: Contains everyone's personal files and app settings.

rules.title: {name}'s user profile
rules.what: Personal files and settings for the Windows user '{name}'.
rules.why: This is personal data — check each item before deleting.

rules.title: Public folder
rules.what: Files shared between all accounts on this PC (and Public Desktop shortcuts).
rules.why: May contain shared files.

rules.title: Default profile template
rules.what: Template copied when a new Windows account is created.
rules.why: Windows needs it to create accounts.

rules.title: Your registry hive
rules.what: Your personal part of the Windows registry: every app setting and preference.
rules.why: Deleting it would wipe your Windows account settings.

rules.title: {name}
rules.what: Your {name} folder — personal files.
rules.why: Only you know what's in here that matters. Large or old files are the best place to free space by hand.
rules.note: Use 'Move to Recycle Bin' so you can undo mistakes.

rules.title: Downloads
rules.what: Everything you've downloaded from the browser, Telegram, WhatsApp and other apps.
rules.why: Often full of installers, zip files and one-off files you no longer need — a classic place to free space.
rules.note: Review before deleting; use Move to Recycle Bin.

rules.title: Downloaded installers
rules.what: A setup program you downloaded. Once the app is installed, the installer isn't needed — you can always download the latest version again.
rules.why: Not needed after installing.

rules.title: Downloaded archives & disk images
rules.what: A compressed archive or disk image you downloaded. Often it has already been extracted somewhere else, so this copy is redundant.
rules.why: Only needed if you haven't extracted it, or want to keep the original.
rules.note: Check you've extracted what you need first.

rules.title: {name} (synced cloud folder)
rules.what: Files synced with OneDrive. Files marked 'online-only' take no space on this PC.
rules.why: Deleting a file here deletes it from OneDrive on all your devices too!
rules.note: To free space without deleting anything: right-click the folder in Explorer → 'Free up space'. Files stay in the cloud.

rules.title: AppData (hidden app data)
rules.what: Hidden folder where apps keep your settings, logins, caches and downloaded content. Local = this PC only, Roaming = follows your account, LocalLow = sandboxed apps.
rules.why: Mixed: some of it is valuable (settings, saves, logins), a lot is cache. Look at individual subfolders — SpaceScope labels the cache ones.

rules.title: {name} (app data)
rules.what: Settings and data stored by {name}.
rules.why: Holds {name}'s settings, logins and local data. If {name} is uninstalled, this is likely a leftover.
rules.note: Deleting it resets {name} as if freshly installed. Check the subfolders — caches inside are labelled separately.

rules.title: Your temporary files
rules.what: Scratch files apps create while installing, updating, extracting archives or rendering. Most apps forget to clean up after themselves.
rules.why: Not needed once the app that made them is closed.
rules.note: Anything currently in use is skipped automatically.

rules.title: Programs (installed just for you)
rules.what: Apps installed for your account only — e.g. VS Code, Discord, Python, Ollama.
rules.why: These are installed apps. Uninstall from Settings → Apps.

rules.title: {name} (installed program)
rules.what: Program files of {name}, installed for your account.
rules.why: Needed to run {name}.
rules.note: Uninstall from Settings → Apps instead of deleting.

rules.title: Store app data
rules.what: Per-app data folders for Microsoft Store and built-in Windows apps.
rules.why: Holds settings and content for each Store app.

rules.title: {name} (Store app data)
rules.what: Settings, caches and local content of a Microsoft Store app.
rules.why: Reset the app via Settings → Apps → Advanced options if needed, rather than deleting.

rules.title: Store app temp/cache
rules.what: Temporary and cached web files of a Store app.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: App execution aliases
rules.what: Tiny shortcut files that let you run Store apps (python, winget, wt) from a command line.
rules.why: Needed for those commands to work.

rules.title: Internet cache (Windows/Office)
rules.what: Web content cached by Windows components, Office and older apps.
rules.why: Re-downloaded when needed.

rules.title: Thumbnail & icon cache
rules.what: Thumbnails Explorer generated for your photos and videos, and the icon cache.
rules.why: Rebuilt as you browse folders.
rules.note: Explorer keeps some of these files open, so a few will be skipped.

rules.title: Windows web cache database
rules.what: Database used by Windows and the old Internet Explorer engine for history and cookies.
rules.why: Locked while Windows runs; leave it.

rules.title: GPU shader cache
rules.what: Compiled graphics shaders saved by DirectX and your GPU driver so games load faster.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically — games may stutter briefly the first time you play after clearing.

rules.title: App crash dumps
rules.what: Memory dumps written when an app crashed.
rules.why: Only useful to a developer debugging the crash.

rules.title: Crash dump files
rules.what: A memory snapshot from a crashed program.
rules.why: Only useful for debugging that crash.

rules.title: Leftover temporary files
rules.what: A temporary file an app left behind.
rules.why: Normally deleted by the app that made it; leftovers are junk.
rules.note: If the app that made it is still open, it is skipped.

rules.title: Icon cache
rules.what: Cached icons for Explorer.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: App updater leftovers
rules.what: Update packages downloaded by Squirrel-based apps (Discord, Slack, Teams classic…).
rules.why: Not needed after the update is applied.

rules.title: {parent} cache
rules.what: Files {parent} downloaded or generated to load faster: web content, images, compiled scripts or GPU shaders.
rules.why: Pure cache — the app rebuilds it automatically. Nothing you made or saved is stored here.
rules.note: Close the app first so files in use can be removed too.

rules.title: {parent} logs
rules.what: Diagnostic logs and crash reports written by {parent}.
rules.why: Only useful when troubleshooting {parent}.

rules.title: {parent} temporary files
rules.what: Scratch space used by {parent}.
rules.why: Not needed when {parent} is closed.

rules.title: Browser profile data
rules.what: Your browser profiles: bookmarks, saved passwords, history, cookies (logins), extensions — plus caches.
rules.why: Deleting the whole folder logs you out of everything and loses bookmarks/passwords not synced to your account.
rules.note: The cache subfolders inside are safe to clear — SpaceScope lists them in Clean up.

rules.title: Website offline storage (service workers)
rules.what: Scripts and cached content websites store so they load fast and work offline (YouTube, Google Docs, WhatsApp Web…).
rules.why: Sites rebuild it on next visit. You stay logged in.
rules.note: Close the browser first for a complete clean.

rules.title: Browser cache
rules.what: Images, scripts and pages the browser saved so websites load faster.
rules.why: Pure cache. Clearing it doesn't log you out or remove bookmarks/passwords — sites just load a bit slower the first time.
rules.note: Close the browser first for a complete clean.

rules.title: Website data (IndexedDB / storage)
rules.what: Data websites store in your browser: offline mail, drafts, web-app databases, settings.
rules.why: Clearing it can log you out of some sites and remove offline data. Prefer the browser's own 'Clear site data'.

rules.title: Browser on-device AI model
rules.what: A local AI model (e.g. Gemini Nano) the browser downloaded for features like 'Help me write'. Usually ~2–4 GB.
rules.why: The browser re-downloads it unless you turn the feature off (chrome://flags → Optimization Guide On Device Model → Disabled).

rules.title: Browser crash reports & update cache
rules.what: Crash reports, component update packages and old profile snapshots.
rules.why: The browser re-creates what it needs.

rules.title: Firefox profile
rules.what: Your Firefox bookmarks, passwords, history, extensions and cookies.
rules.why: Personal data — don't delete.

rules.title: Firefox cache
rules.what: Web pages and images Firefox cached.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: Discord app data
rules.what: Discord's settings, login and caches.
rules.why: Deleting it logs you out of Discord. Its Cache folders are safe to clear.

rules.title: Discord app version ({name})
rules.what: An installed Discord version. Discord keeps the previous version next to the current one.
rules.why: Only the newest app-* folder is used.

rules.title: Spotify streaming cache
rules.what: Songs Spotify cached so they play instantly. Can grow to 10 GB.
rules.why: Re-downloaded when you play them. (Downloaded playlists may need re-downloading.)
rules.note: You can cap its size in Spotify → Settings → Storage.

rules.title: Telegram media cache
rules.what: Photos, videos, stickers and voice messages Telegram cached as you scrolled chats.
rules.why: Everything stays in the cloud and is re-downloaded when you open it.
rules.note: Better: Telegram → Settings → Advanced → Manage local storage → Clear all.

rules.title: Telegram downloads
rules.what: Files you saved from Telegram chats.
rules.why: They're still in the chats (unless deleted there), but these copies may be the only local ones.

rules.title: WhatsApp media & cache
rules.what: Media WhatsApp Desktop downloaded from your chats.
rules.why: Media may not be re-downloadable if it was deleted from your phone.

rules.title: Microsoft Teams cache
rules.what: Teams' embedded browser cache.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically; you may need to sign in again.

rules.title: Zoom data
rules.what: Zoom settings and local chat data.
rules.why: Holds your Zoom login and preferences.

rules.title: Outlook offline mailbox
rules.what: A local copy of your mailbox so Outlook works offline. Can be tens of GB.
rules.why: Outlook rebuilds it from the server, but that can take hours. Shrink it instead: Account settings → 'Download email for the past' 1 year.
rules.note: Never delete .pst files — those are archives that exist only on this PC.

rules.title: Office document cache
rules.what: Local copies of cloud documents Office opened, and telemetry.
rules.why: Rebuilt from OneDrive/SharePoint.

rules.title: OneDrive app
rules.what: The OneDrive sync program and its logs.
rules.why: Needed for syncing.

rules.title: Google Drive cache
rules.what: Google Drive for desktop's local content cache of streamed files.
rules.why: Files stay in Drive. Clear it from Drive's settings (gear → Preferences → Local cached files → Clear) rather than deleting.

rules.title: iPhone / iPad backups
rules.what: Full backups of an iPhone or iPad made by iTunes / Apple Devices. Each can be tens of GB.
rules.why: May be your only backup of that phone. Old backups of phones you no longer own are safe to remove.
rules.note: Each subfolder is one device backup. Check the dates.

rules.title: Adobe media cache
rules.what: Conformed audio (.cfa), peak waveforms (.pek) and indexed video Premiere Pro, After Effects and Media Encoder create for every clip you import. Grows without limit.
rules.why: Regenerated automatically when you open a project — the first open will be slower.
rules.note: Close Adobe apps first. You can set automatic cleanup in Preferences → Media Cache.

rules.title: After Effects disk cache
rules.what: Rendered frames After Effects saves so previews play back instantly. Can easily be 50–100 GB.
rules.why: Only speeds up previews; AE re-renders what it needs.
rules.note: Best cleared from AE: Edit → Purge → All Memory & Disk Cache.

rules.title: Adobe temporary files
rules.what: Scratch files Adobe apps (Premiere Pro, After Effects, Media Encoder, Creative Cloud) write at the root of the drive.
rules.why: Not needed once the Adobe app is closed.

rules.title: Adobe auto-saves
rules.what: Automatic backup copies of your Premiere / After Effects projects.
rules.why: Your safety net if a project file gets corrupted. Old ones for finished projects can go.

rules.title: Camera Raw cache
rules.what: Previews generated by Camera Raw/Lightroom.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: Lightroom previews
rules.what: Preview images Lightroom Classic generated for your catalog.
rules.why: Rebuilt from the originals. (Smart Previews let you edit offline photos.)

rules.title: DaVinci Resolve render cache
rules.what: Render cache and optimized media generated by DaVinci Resolve.
rules.why: Regenerated from your source footage.

rules.title: CapCut cache
rules.what: Effects, templates, thumbnails and proxy media CapCut downloaded or generated. Frequently 10+ GB.
rules.why: Re-downloaded or regenerated when needed. Your projects are stored separately.

rules.title: CapCut projects
rules.what: Your CapCut project drafts.
rules.why: Your edits. Delete individual old projects from inside CapCut.

rules.title: OBS logs
rules.what: OBS Studio session logs.
rules.why: Troubleshooting only.

rules.title: Steam
rules.what: The Steam client and (by default) your installed Steam games.
rules.why: Uninstall games from inside Steam.

rules.title: Steam games
rules.what: Installed Steam games — each subfolder is one game.
rules.why: Uninstall games you no longer play from Steam (right-click → Manage → Uninstall). Saves are usually in the cloud.

rules.title: {name} (Steam game)
rules.what: The installed game {name}.
rules.why: Needed to play {name}.
rules.note: Uninstall from Steam rather than deleting the folder, so Steam knows it's gone.

rules.title: Steam shader pre-caches
rules.what: Pre-compiled shaders Steam downloads for your games so they don't stutter.
rules.why: Re-downloaded/rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: Steam download/temp files
rules.what: Partial downloads, depot manifests, logs and crash dumps from Steam.
rules.why: Steam re-creates them. Clearing 'downloading' cancels any paused download.

rules.title: Steam Workshop content
rules.what: Mods and maps you subscribed to in the Steam Workshop.
rules.why: Re-downloaded if you stay subscribed; unsubscribe in Steam to remove for good.

rules.title: {name} (Epic Games)
rules.what: A game or tool installed through the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.why: Uninstall from the Epic Games Launcher.

rules.title: {name} (Xbox / Game Pass)
rules.what: A game installed from the Xbox app / Game Pass.
rules.why: Uninstall from the Xbox app or Settings → Apps.

rules.title: {name} (games)
rules.what: Games installed through a launcher.
rules.why: Uninstall through the launcher that installed them.

rules.title: Minecraft (Java) data
rules.what: Your Minecraft worlds (saves), mods, resource packs and game files.
rules.why: Saves folder holds your singleplayer worlds — back up before deleting anything.

rules.title: node_modules (JavaScript packages)
rules.what: Third-party JavaScript packages downloaded for a project by npm/yarn/pnpm. Often hundreds of MB per project.
rules.why: Fully re-creatable with `npm install` — but delete only for projects you're not actively working on.
rules.note: Nothing you wrote lives here. Re-run `npm install` in the project to restore.

rules.title: Rust build output (target)
rules.what: Compiled build artifacts from cargo. Tauri and Rust projects easily reach 2–10 GB each.
rules.why: Rebuilt by `cargo build` (the next build will take a few minutes).

rules.title: Python bytecode cache
rules.what: Compiled .pyc files and tool caches Python creates automatically.
rules.why: Regenerated the next time the code runs.

rules.title: Python virtual environment
rules.what: An isolated Python installation with a project's packages (torch alone is 2–4 GB).
rules.why: Re-creatable with `pip install -r requirements.txt`, if the project has one.

rules.title: Build cache ({name})
rules.what: Build output/cache of a web or app framework.
rules.why: Rebuilt on the next build or dev-server start.

rules.title: Visual Studio solution cache (.vs)
rules.what: IntelliSense database and per-user state for a Visual Studio solution.
rules.why: Rebuilt when the solution is opened.

rules.title: Git repository history
rules.what: The complete version history of a code project.
rules.why: If the project isn't pushed anywhere, this is the only copy of its history.

rules.title: JavaScript package cache
rules.what: Downloaded packages kept by npm, Yarn, Bun, node-gyp or Electron so installs are faster.
rules.why: Re-downloaded automatically when a project needs them.

rules.title: pnpm package store
rules.what: pnpm's shared package store. Projects hard-link into it, so it is often smaller than it looks.
rules.why: Run `pnpm store prune` instead — it only removes packages no project uses.

rules.title: Python package cache
rules.what: Downloaded wheels and packages kept by pip, uv, poetry or conda (`conda clean --all` does the same).
rules.why: Re-downloaded when needed.

rules.title: Rust crate cache
rules.what: Downloaded and unpacked crates from crates.io.
rules.why: Re-downloaded on the next build.

rules.title: Rust toolchains
rules.what: Installed Rust compilers. Each toolchain is ~1 GB.
rules.why: Remove unused ones with `rustup toolchain uninstall <name>`.

rules.title: Developer package/build cache
rules.what: Dependencies and build caches downloaded by Gradle, Maven, NuGet, Go, Composer, Unity or JetBrains IDEs.
rules.why: Re-downloaded or re-indexed automatically.

rules.title: Android SDK / emulators
rules.what: Android SDK platforms, system images and emulator disks. System images are 1–5 GB each.
rules.why: Remove unused ones from Android Studio's SDK Manager / Device Manager.

rules.title: Automation browsers (Playwright / Puppeteer)
rules.what: Headless browser builds downloaded by Playwright, Puppeteer or Remotion.
rules.why: Re-downloaded on next use.

rules.title: VS Code cache
rules.what: Cached extension installers, compiled code, logs and per-workspace state.
rules.why: Rebuilt automatically (workspace state like open tabs is reset).

rules.title: Editor extensions
rules.what: Installed VS Code / Cursor extensions.
rules.why: Remove unused ones from the editor's Extensions panel.

rules.title: Visual Studio cache
rules.what: MEF component cache and telemetry of Visual Studio.
rules.why: Rebuilt on start.

rules.title: Hugging Face model cache
rules.what: AI models and datasets downloaded by Python libraries (transformers, diffusers, rembg, Whisper…). Individual models are often 1–20 GB.
rules.why: Re-downloaded automatically the next time an app needs them — but that can be slow and large. Delete models you no longer use.
rules.note: Each models--org--name subfolder is one model.

rules.title: AI model downloads
rules.what: Model weights downloaded by PyTorch, Whisper, rembg (u2net), CLIP or LM Studio.
rules.why: Re-downloaded on next use.

rules.title: Tool cache (.cache)
rules.what: A shared cache folder used by developer and AI tools.
rules.why: Mostly re-downloadable, but check what's inside — large items are usually AI models.

rules.title: Ollama AI models
rules.what: Local language models used by Ollama (e.g. qwen3, llama). Each is 2–40 GB.
rules.why: Your local AI apps need them. Remove unused models with `ollama rm <name>` (see `ollama list`) instead of deleting files.

rules.title: LM Studio models
rules.what: Local language models downloaded in LM Studio.
rules.why: Delete unused models from LM Studio's 'My Models' tab.

rules.title: Image-generation models
rules.what: Stable Diffusion / Flux checkpoints, LoRAs and VAEs. 2–25 GB each.
rules.why: Needed to generate images; delete models you don't use.

rules.title: Docker Desktop disk
rules.what: Virtual disk holding all Docker images, containers and volumes. It grows but never shrinks on its own.
rules.why: Contains your containers and volumes. Free space with `docker system prune -a`, then Docker Desktop → Troubleshoot → Clean / Purge data.

rules.title: WSL Linux disk
rules.what: The virtual hard disk (ext4.vhdx) of a WSL Linux distribution — your whole Linux file system.
rules.why: Deleting it deletes your Linux install and files. It doesn't shrink automatically; compact it with `wsl --manage <distro> --set-sparse true`.

rules.title: Virtual machines
rules.what: Virtual machine disks (Hyper-V / VirtualBox / VMware).
rules.why: Each disk is a whole computer. Delete VMs you don't use from the VM manager.

rules.title: Package manager download cache
rules.what: Installers kept by Scoop/Chocolatey after installing.
rules.why: Re-downloaded if needed (`scoop cache rm *`).

rules.title: Launcher/installer cache
rules.what: Installer files and web caches kept by game launchers and setup programs.
rules.why: Re-downloaded if needed.
